document.title: Iron Ridge Middle Elective Course Guide

credit_by_exam.rule: Currently, a student may earn high school credit in Algebra I, Geometry, U.S. History or Biology I if the student passes the statewide, standardized end-of-course (EOC) assessment with a level 3 or higher without the requirement of enrolling in or completing the course.
credit_by_exam.note: Three of the four are also taught here as courses — GEM-7 is Algebra I Honors, GEM-8 is Geometry Honors, and the GEARS sequence ends in Honors Biology 1. Only U.S. History is not taught at this school at any level, so for that one the exam is the only route.

courses.title: 3D Art
courses.credit_note: Middle school courses carry no credit.

prerequisites.raw: required to complete Art I prior to enrolling

courses.description: 3-D ART (8th Grade Elective) Students are required to complete Art I prior to enrolling in 3-D Art. This course highlights artists and art history as sources of inspiration for various art projects. Students will craft both two-dimensional and three-dimensional works. Students will have the chance to make personal decisions regarding their artistic creations.

courses.title: Art I
courses.credit_note: Middle school courses carry no credit.
courses.description: Introductory Art, or Art I, provides students with a foundational understanding of key art elements like color, line, value, form, space, shape, and texture. By the end, students will gain insights into the potential of art, laying a strong foundation for future artistic endeavors.

courses.title: Art II
courses.credit_note: Middle school courses carry no credit.

prerequisites.raw: required to complete Art I prior to enrolling

courses.description: Students are required to complete Art I prior to enrolling in Art II. Students experiment with various media, techniques, and methods. Projects will concentrate on enhancing the elements of art (line, form, color, value, texture) and principles of design (balance, variety, harmony, emphasis). Focus on art history, culture, and heritage. Students will create a mix of two-dimensional and threedimensional projects.

data_notes: Middle school carries no credit, so every course here is zero. Four electives — Debate I, Journalism I, Spanish I and Speech I — are marked in the guide as earning high school credit, but the guide does not say how much, so no credit value was invented for them. They carry a `high_school_credit` flag instead.
The guide marks courses with ^ for an application and * for a prerequisite, and defines both keys on the list pages. Those become the `application_required` and `prerequisite_required` flags.

Prerequisites come from two places, and each course records which. Some are stated in the guide's own words — "Students are required to complete Art I prior to enrolling in 3-D Art", "Fundamentals of Finance I prerequisite required", "offered to students that completed Journalism I" — and carry `basis: "stated"`. The band ladder is not: the guide asks for "prior years of experience playing a band instrument" rather than naming a course, so Band II, III and IV are chained on the reading the numbered titles allow, and carry `basis: "inferred"`. Reading only the asterisks on the list pages, and none of the prose, missed three prerequisites the guide states plainly.

The school publishes no course names for English Language Arts, Mathematics, Science or Social Studies. Those four appear once per grade, described in the school's own words from its academic pathways page. They are subjects, not courses, and no course titles were invented for them. Their year-to-year sequence is inferred from the grades.
Teacher names and room numbers printed in the guide have been removed.

A course taken here for high school credit carries two credit values, and they are kept apart. `credits` is zero, because that is what it counts for in middle school. `high_school_credits` is one, because that is what it will count for at the high school it transfers to. Neither guide prints the second value; one credit is what every year-long course carries in the district's own high school catalogue, where 273 of its 280 courses are one credit and the seven exceptions are double-block classes.

Six electives earn high school credit, not four: the guide announces it in the page heading for some and in the body text for others, and Honors Band carries it as an option in eighth grade only. Reading headings alone missed two of them.

The band ladder is printed under two sets of names — Band II, III and IV on the elective lists, Concert, Symphonic and Honors Band on the specialised programmes page. Both are the school's own words, so both resolve, through `title_variants`.

The school publishes no honours version of its ordinary core classes, but it does name two accelerated tracks — GEM in mathematics and GEARS in science — and the district defines both. GEM is Great Explorations in Mathematics: GEM-6 compresses three years of middle school mathematics into one, GEM-7 is Algebra I Honors and GEM-8 is Geometry Honors, the last two for high school credit with a state end-of-course exam worth 30% of the grade. GEARS is Genuine Explorations, Applications and Research in Science, which compresses the science sequence so a high school science course can be taken in eighth grade. Every one of those records names both the school page saying it runs the programme and the district page defining it.

Biology is taught here, at the end of the GEARS sequence: GEARS 1 in sixth grade, GEARS 2 in seventh, then Honors Biology 1 in eighth for high school credit. Iron Ridge names the programme but not its courses, so the course names come from another Braewood middle school's published description of the same sequence. That is a weaker source than the district page behind GEM, and every GEARS record names all three sources so the join can be checked.

Separately from any course, the district allows a middle school pupil to earn high school credit in Algebra I, Geometry, U.S. History or Biology I by passing the state end-of-course exam at level 3 or higher, explicitly without enrolling in or completing the course. That is credit by examination, not a class, so it is recorded in `credit_by_exam` beside the catalogue rather than as courses that do not exist. Anyone looking for a Biology class here will not find one, and that absence is the fact rather than a gap in this file.
GEARS 1 and GEARS 2 are not single-subject courses: each covers part of one year's standards and part of another's, which is how two years of science are compressed into the room for one more.

This is one school's guide. Braewood County publishes no district-wide middle school course catalog; the counseling department points instead at CPALMS and the state course code directory, and notes that not every school offers every course.

The school and the county are fictitious. Iron Ridge Middle School in Braewood County does not exist: the school name, the district name, the mascot and the student newspaper named after it all replaced real ones. The curriculum is unchanged — every course, elective, prerequisite and programme is exactly as the source documents describe it, and the source links have been removed rather than redirected.

State-level references are left alone. Florida, its end-of-course exams and its scholastic press association are a state and its institutions, not the school, and the curriculum does not make sense without them.
